Backs the sentence that the card follows a work authorisation the employer applies for, on fr-salarie (s9). Sliced to the two steps that state it: the fiche carries a favourites dialog, a share menu and a whole site navigation whose wording moves without the rules moving.

slice.from: Comment faire la demande d'autorisation de travail pour pouvoir embaucher un salarié étranger en France ?

entries.note: The employer-side fiche for the autorisation de travail — the test that keeps fr-salarie out of the scoring. Backs the three-week advertisement, the shortage-occupation exemption, the employer's own record, the disproportionate-recruitment refusal, the regulated-profession condition and the Smic-or-agreement pay floor. Sliced from the application section to the end of the pay condition: the whole fiche is 96,000 characters of which the rest is navigation, related fiches and a business-form filter. Legifrance, which states the opposabilité in as many words, answers this fetcher with 403 (measured 2026-09-10), so no s9 quote comes from it. The one Legifrance page this dataset does quote is the Conseil d'État decision behind the Algerian notice, and that one ships human-tier, re-read by a person every 90 days.

entries.note: RD 1155/2024, the immigration regulation, consolidated. Backs every condition on es-cuenta-ajena (arts. 73–76). Sliced to those four articles: the consolidated page is 750,000 characters and carries the whole regulation plus a per-article modification history. The BOE's consolidated PDF of the same text is NOT usable here — this project's decoder returns stream and font noise for it, not words (measured 2026-09-10, s9).

entries.note: The federal office's own article for § 21, in English. Backs the business-plan sentence on de-selbstaendige-taetigkeit — the authority saying in its own words what the statute's Beurteilung is made from. Sliced to the article body: this page ends with a rotating public-tender announcement ("Aufforderung zur Abgabe einer Interessenbekundung") that has nothing to do with the route, and the four older bamf entries hash it (s9).

entries.note: Wet arbeid vreemdelingen art. 8 — the article that writes the refusal of the single permit itself. Backs the labour-market ground on nl-gvva. Sliced to article 8 lid 1, and the slice is not optional: the statute book prints the day it was consulted ("Geraadpleegd op …") on every request, so an unsliced entry would report a change every single day. The undated URL is deliberate — it serves the version in force, and a route page quoting a superseded one would be quoting a law nobody is under. The address is the undated one on purpose: wetten.overheid.nl serves the law as it stands there, while the dated form the research quoted (/2024-01-01) is a frozen version that can never change — and a source that cannot change is a watch that can never fire.

The benefits agency's own page for an ordinary vacancy. Backs the three-month European search, the five-week vacancy report, the agency's own sentence that it is the one that checks, the account of the selection, and the 90-day boundary between the two Dutch work permits, all on nl-gvva. Unsliced: the whole page is 4,000 characters and is the article, with no chrome that moves (s9). Watched whole rather than sliced: after normalisation the page is 3–7 KB and is operative text end to end — there is no menu region to cut, so a slice would only be a second thing to keep in step (Spec review, 2026-09-10).

The four general conditions of a Dutch work permit, and the five-year labour-law fine. Backs both on nl-gvva. Unsliced for the reason above: 2,900 characters, all of it the article. Watched whole rather than sliced: after normalisation the page is 3–7 KB and is operative text end to end — there is no menu region to cut, so a slice would only be a second thing to keep in step (Spec review, 2026-09-10).

Who needs no work permit at all. Backs the two carve-outs stated on nl-gvva — the highly skilled migrant permit this site does score, and a residence permit that already allows free work. Unsliced: 7,300 characters, all of it the article. Watched whole rather than sliced: after normalisation the page is 3–7 KB and is operative text end to end — there is no menu region to cut, so a slice would only be a second thing to keep in step (Spec review, 2026-09-10).

slice.from: You are a citizen of the Union if you are a national of one of the member states of the European Union (EU).
slice.to: Your employer does not need a work permit (in Dutch: tewerkstellingsvergunning or TWV).

entries.note: IND's general page for EU, EEA and Swiss citizens. Backs the EEA sentence on the eu-free-movement notice — the one that puts Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway on the same footing as an EU passport (data #15: the notice named five groups and quoted a sentence covering one). Not one of the five form-walled route pages: measured 2026-09-17 with this watch's client, HTTP 200, 51,875 bytes, the sentence in the visible prose. Sliced from the 'citizen of the Union' sentence to the end of the 'Working in the Netherlands' paragraph: the page's own "Last update" date sits above the slice, and ind.nl has answered a bare fetch from this host with an app shell (2026-09-07) — a shell carries no marker, so it reports unreachable and the snapshot stands, instead of a change that would put this quote into `missing`.

The Opportunity Card's "Official page" (de-chancenkarte.info_url) since 2026-09-17: the Federal Ministry of the Interior's own English notice on the card, where the route's quotes and the reader's door were on different sites before (data #13). Backs no value — the route's sentences are quoted from the Cairo leaflet and the statute — so it is a sentinel: what this entry watches is that the page a reader is sent to still exists, carrying "The opportunity card is a new type of residence permit for those coming to Germany to look for work." Browser tier because the page is served only after a cookie round-trip: measured 2026-09-17 with this watch's client, the URL answers HTTP 307 to /cookie-check-d973 and sets an AL_CHK-S cookie, and this fetcher keeps no cookie jar, so it lands on an HTTP 400 "Zugriff nicht möglich" (re-measured 2026-09-23: still HTTP 400, 858 bytes). A browser keeps the cookie without being asked — measured 2026-09-23, headless Chrome renders the notice, 125 kB of HTML and the sentinel sentence in place. No steps: nothing has to be answered or opened, only kept. Sliced to the notice's own body, from its requirements heading to the end of the article, so the ministry's rotating press-release teasers above it do not flag a page that has not moved.

history.note: Entry born with the move of de-chancenkarte.info_url from https://handbookgermany.de/en/opportunity-card to this page (data #13, s29). The old page was a federally funded guide, not the authority; handbookgermany.de was never watched, so this line is the only dated record of the move — a route's info_url is a bare string in the schema, with no history of its own. Candidates read the same day and passed over: make-it-in-germany.com (a bot-check shell on a plain GET), digital.diplo.de (a JavaScript shell), bamf.de and the Foreign Office (no Chancenkarte page found, 404), buzer.de (the statute, already the route's source).

Strategy moved from `human` to `browser` and the verification age removed, and the entry gained a slice (s34). The cookie round-trip this fetcher cannot make is one a browser makes without being asked; the note's own "what would move it to the machine" line of 2026-09-17 is what this slice did.
